nodes.name: Pulsed Laser Deposition and RTA
nodes.procedure: The confined NiFe NPs catalysts were prepared on glassy carbon electrode substrates by PLD technique combined with a RTA process. First, the permalloy (NiFe) (99.9%) and carbon (99.9%) targets were alternately ablated by KrF pulsed laser (248 nm) under ultra-high vacuum conditions (≈5×10^{-8} Torr). The laser energy was 300 mJ and the frequency was 10 Hz with a pulse width of 10 ns. During the deposition, both NiFe/carbon target and substrate rotated slowly around their central axis. After 5 min of PLD deposition, the NiFe NPs composites were rapidly thermal annealed at 400°C for 5 min under Ar atmosphere at 100 sccm.

nodes.name: In situ Electrochemical Reconstruction
nodes.procedure: The synthesis of NiFe/NiFeOOH core/shell NPs was achieved by EC-reconstruction based on PLD-prepared confined NiFe NPs on glassy carbon electrode. This was conducted using a three-electrode system (CHI 760E electrochemical workstation) with NiFe NPs as working electrode, saturated Hg/HgO as reference electrode, and graphite rod as counter electrode. The in situ EC-reconstruction was performed by cyclic voltammetry (CV) at a scan rate of 50 mV s⁻¹ for 40 cycles in the potential range of 1.0 to 1.8 V vs RHE in 1.0 M KOH electrolyte.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-density NiFe NPs with good homogeneity and average diameter ≈9 nm are confined in amorphous carbon matrix.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2a, the typical low-resolution TEM (LRTEM) image implies that high-density NiFe NPs with a good homogeneity were successfully confined in an amorphous carbon matrix. These monodispersed NiFe NPs present spherical nanostructures with an average diameter of ≈9 nm (the inset of Figure 2a).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern matches cubic NiFe structure with space group Fm3m.
nodes.evidence_snippet: By matching the simulated electron diffraction pattern produced by TEM Java electron microscopy simulation (JEMS) software with the corresponding selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of NiFe NPs (Figure 2b), it can be concluded that the crystal structure of the NiFe NPs is a cubic structure with a space group of Fm3m.

nodes.characterization_summary: Single crystalline NiFe NP shows lattice spacing of 0.18 nm corresponding to (200) plane of cubic NiFe alloy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2c shows the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image of a representative single NiFe NP, displaying a single crystallinity with lattice spacing of 0.18 nm, which can be related to the crystallographic (200) plane of cubic NiFe alloy.

nodes.characterization_summary: All XRD patterns indexed to permalloy with cubic structure (JCPDS No. 47-1417).
nodes.evidence_snippet: All of the XRD pattern in Figure S1, Supporting Information, can be indexed to a permalloy with cubic structure (JCPDS No. 47-1417), in agreement with the TEM results.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni:Fe content ratio measured as 1:1 with homogeneous distribution of Ni, Fe, and C elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S2, Supporting Information, the homogeneous distribution of Ni, Fe, and C elements in the PLD-prepared NiFe NPs indicated the compact confined nanostructure and the Ni:Fe content ratio was measured as 1:1.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p peaks at 869.9 eV (2p1/2) and 852.7 eV (2p3/2); Fe 2p peaks at 719.8 eV (2p1/2) and 706.6 eV (2p3/2) confirm metallic Ni0 and Fe0.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Ni 2p region (Figure S3a, Supporting Information), the doublet peaks located at 869.9 and 852.7 eV can be assigned to Ni0 2p1/2 and Ni0 2p3/2, respectively. The additional doublet peaks located at 719.8 and 706.6 eV in the Fe 2p region (Figure S3b, Supporting Information), correspond to the Fe0 2p1/2 and Fe0 2p3/2, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Room-temperature superparamagnetism confirmed by s-like M-H curve without coercivity at 300K.
nodes.evidence_snippet: And an s-like hysteresis without coercivity was observed in the magnetization versus magnetic field (M-H) curve at 300K (Figure 2d), indicating the room-temperature superparamagnetism of NiFe NPs.

nodes.characterization_summary: Core/shell nanostructured NPs clearly observed with average size about 11 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2e shows the representative low-resolution TEM (LRTEM) image of the reconstructed NPs, in which the core/shell nanostructured NPs are clearly observed. And the average size of NPs after EC-reconstruction is about 11 nm (the inset of Figure 2e)...

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern of core/shell NPs matches cubic NiFe, indicating retention of NiFe core.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2f shows the corresponding SAED pattern of the core/shell NPs. The SAED pattern matches well with simulated electron diffraction pattern of cubic NiFe NPs, indicating the retention of NiFe core in the reconstructed NPs.

nodes.characterization_summary: Core/shell NP shows highly crystalline core and 1.52 nm amorphous shell with 0.18 nm lattice spacing of NiFe (200) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the HRTEM image in Figure 2g shows a typical core/shell NP, displaying a highly crystalline core and an ultra-thin (about 1.52 nm) amorphous shell. The lattice stripes of the core exhibit the same 0.18 nm plane spacing as previous NiFe NPs...

nodes.characterization_summary: No obvious differences in diffraction pattern between reconstructed core/shell NPs and NiFe NPs, confirming amorphous NiFeOOH shell.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S7, Supporting Information, no obvious differences in the diffraction pattern are observed between the reconstructed core/shell NPs with the NiFe NPs, suggesting the amorphous feature of the formed NiFe-derived (oxy)hydroxides shell.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p peaks at 856.4 eV (2p3/2) and 874.2 eV (2p1/2) for Ni3+; Fe 2p peaks at 712.5 eV (2p3/2) and 725.6 eV (2p1/2) for Fe3+; O 1s peaks confirm NiFeOOH shell.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p region (Figure S8a, Supporting Information), shows two doublet peaks located at 856.4 and 874.2 eV, which can be assigned to Ni 2p3/2 and Ni 2p1/2 of Ni3+. The Fe 2p region (Figure S8b, Supporting Information), presents two peaks at 712.5 and 725.6 eV... The XPS results reveal that the EC-reconstructed amorphous shell is NiFeOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe/NiFeOOH core/shell NPs exhibit room-temperature superparamagnetism with s-like M-H behavior without coercivity at 300K.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The 300K s-like M-H behavior without coercivity behavior in Figure 2h indicates that NiFe/NiFeOOH core/shell NPs is superparamagnetic.

nodes.characterization_summary: Single NiFe/NiFeOOH core/shell NP after 16h OER operation shows unchanged morphology and lattice structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The representative HRTEM image of a single NiFe/NiFeOOH core/shell NPs after long-term electrochemical operation clearly shows that the morphology and lattice structure have not changed (as shown in Figure 5b).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern after long-term OER matches simulated cubic NiFe alloy pattern, confirming structural stability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 5c shows the SAED pattern, which is well matched the simulated electron diffraction pattern of cubic NiFe alloy.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS spectra of NiFe/NiFeOOH after 16h OER show no significant peak shift or intensity change.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 5d–f shows the spectrum of NiFe/NiFeOOH core/shell NPs after the 16h durability test. The XPS results show that the XPS peaks do not show a significant shift and change in intensity.

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrolyte after long-term operation shows no detectable Fe or Ni leaching signals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In stark contrast to the two distinct peaks located at 259.941 and 231.604 nm... the ICP-AES characterization of our electrolyte after long-term operation exhibits undistinguished signal at the corresponding wavelength. This indicates that there is no detachment of FeOOH or NiOOH during the long-term operation.
